checklist.step: Refresh the written supervisory procedures for variable annuity sales
actions: Re-read the VA sections of the written supervisory procedures against FINRA Rules 3110, 3120, 2330 and Reg BI, and record the date and reviewer on the document header.
Name in the procedures the supervising principal for each branch and office of supervisory jurisdiction, with a designated alternate.
State the numeric sampling rates, the senior-investor 100% rule and the exchange-velocity thresholds so the test is reproducible by a third party.
Amend the procedures within 30 days of any new variable product, branch opening or change of supervising principal.
checklist.done: the WSP carries a dated review, a named principal per branch, numeric sampling rates and a 30-day amendment record.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly transaction population
actions: Run the quarterly extract on the first business day after quarter end joining VA transactions to customer demographics, funding source, branch, representative CRD and the suitability review record.
Include new sales, 1035 exchanges, replacements and subsequent purchase payments — subsequent payments are the most commonly omitted category.
Derive customer age at the transaction date rather than reading a stored senior flag, and derive tenure of the representative in variable-product selling.
Reconcile the row count to the issued-contract file and the commission ledger and publish the reconciliation alongside the extract.
checklist.done: a reconciled quarterly population exists on the first business day after quarter end with derived age and representative tenure.

checklist.step: Risk-rank the population before sampling
actions: Score every transaction on the documented risk factors: owner or annuitant aged 65+, 1035 exchange, exchange within 36 months of a prior exchange, surrender charge incurred, premium above 50% of stated liquid net worth, reverse-mortgage or home-equity funding, and a representative with a prior finding.
Publish the ranked list with the score components visible so a reviewer can see why a row scored high.
Compute branch-level and representative-level concentration metrics — exchange rate, average surrender charge incurred, senior share of premium.
Hand the ranked list and the concentration metrics to the Compliance Manager with the outliers named.
checklist.done: every transaction carries a visible risk score and branch and representative concentration metrics are published with outliers named.

checklist.step: Run the Rule 2330(d) exchange surveillance thresholds
actions: Compute per representative: the number of VA exchanges in the quarter, the exchange share of their VA transactions, and the count of customers exchanged within 36 months of a prior exchange.
Apply the thresholds stated in SUP-3120 and list every representative who breaches one, with the transactions behind the breach.
Compare each breaching representative to their prior four quarters to distinguish a spike from a standing pattern.
Escalate every threshold breach to the supervising principal with a written request for explanation inside 5 business days.
checklist.done: exchange-velocity thresholds are computed per representative, breaches are listed with underlying transactions and escalated for written explanation.

checklist.step: Draw the quarterly supervisory sample
actions: Take 100% of transactions in the senior-investor stratum (owner or annuitant 65+) and 100% of exchange-velocity threshold breaches.
Take 100% of transactions from representatives with an open finding or a heightened-supervision plan.
Take a seeded random sample of the remaining population at the rate stated in SUP-3120, with each branch represented at least once.
Record the seed, strata counts, population size and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn identically.
checklist.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers every senior transaction, threshold breach and open-finding representative.

checklist.step: Review each sampled transaction against the best-interest standard
actions: Open the sampled ticket and read the customer profile, the source of funds, the exchange worksheet and the product features before reading the original conclusion.
Test the Rule 2111 customer-specific and quantitative factors and the Reg BI care obligation, and record whether the recommendation remains defensible on the facts as documented.
Check that the file evidences the customer's need for the specific features paid for — tax deferral, annuitization, a death benefit or a living benefit.
Assign a disposition code — Satisfactory, Documentation Defect, Supervisory Finding or Suitability Concern — with a typed reason.
Escalate every Suitability Concern to the Compliance Manager the same day.
checklist.done: every sampled transaction has an independent review note, a disposition code and a typed reason, with concerns escalated same day.

checklist.step: Apply the senior-investor heightened review module to the 65+ stratum
actions: For every 65+ transaction, re-test the source of funds, the liquidity position after purchase, the stated time horizon against the surrender-charge duration, and the annuity concentration against the 50% liquid-net-worth limit.
Confirm the Senior Investor Worksheet is signed by a registered principal and that the reason the product stays in the customer's best interest is specific to the customer, not boilerplate.
Check the trusted contact field under Rule 4512(a)(1)(F) and any recorded capacity or undue-influence observation, and confirm any red flag produced a Rule 2165 hold decision.
Where the surrender period ends beyond the customer's age 85, confirm a written statement explains why the funds are not needed inside that period.
Log any 65+ transaction failing these tests as a Supervisory Finding regardless of dollar size.
checklist.done: each 65+ transaction is re-tested on funds, liquidity, horizon, concentration and capacity, with failures logged as supervisory findings.

checklist.step: Correlate complaints and rescissions with the sampled representatives
actions: Extract the quarter's customer complaints, free-look cancellations and early surrenders on variable products by representative CRD and branch.
Match them to the sampled representatives and add any representative with two or more complaints in the quarter to the sample regardless of risk score.
Read the complaint narratives for recurring themes — a misunderstood surrender charge, an unexpected rider cost, a promise of guaranteed return — and record the theme.
Confirm every reportable complaint was recorded for FINRA Rule 4530 reporting and reflected on the representative's Form U4 where required.
checklist.done: complaints, free-look cancellations and early surrenders are matched to representatives, themes recorded, and Rule 4530 reporting confirmed.

checklist.step: Conduct the branch and OSJ inspection module
actions: For branches flagged by defect rate or complaint volume, run the Rule 3110(c) inspection covering safeguarding of customer funds, customer account records, supervisory review of transactions and correspondence, and the handling of customer complaints.
Interview the supervising principal on how they evidence their Rule 2330(c) reviews and how they handle a returned ticket.
Test five customer files on site end to end — application, suitability form, disclosure receipts, principal approval, complaint history.
Write a dated inspection report naming the branch, the principal, the tests performed, the findings and the remediation dates.
checklist.done: each flagged branch has a dated Rule 3110(c) inspection report with tests performed, findings and remediation dates.

checklist.step: Open heightened supervision on representatives with a pattern
actions: Open a plan on any representative with three or more findings in a rolling four quarters, a threshold breach unexplained after 5 business days, or a Suitability Concern involving a senior investor.
Name in the plan the supervising principal, the pre-approval requirement on all future VA business, the elevated correspondence sampling rate and the review period.
Notify the representative and the branch manager in writing and record their acknowledgement.
Set a formal exit test at the end of the review period — a clean 100% review of that period's transactions — before the plan closes.
checklist.done: every pattern representative sits under a written plan with a named principal, pre-approval requirement, review period and an exit test.

checklist.step: Feed findings back into the suitability desk and the training programme
actions: Summarise the quarter's disposition mix and the top three defect causes and send them to the Suitability Desk and the Learning Development Manager.
Where a defect is systemic — a profile field routinely left blank, an exchange worksheet routinely unquantified — change the form or the system validation rather than issuing a reminder.
Feed the top defect causes into the next Firm Element needs analysis as named topics.
Record the change made and the date so the next quarter's test can measure whether it worked.
checklist.done: the quarter's top defect causes are fed to training and the desk, with a recorded systemic fix and a date for measurement.

checklist.step: Track remediation of every open finding to closure
actions: Confirm every finding has a GRC issue carrying the contract number, representative CRD, branch, rule implicated, root cause, owner and remediation date.
Chase owners at 15 and 25 days past quarter end and escalate anything unclosed at 30 days to the Head of Compliance.
Confirm customer-impacting findings carry a customer remediation decision — re-papering, fee reimbursement or rescission — cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open finding into the next quarter's sample as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every finding has a complete GRC record, a chased owner, a customer-impact decision where relevant and a retest commitment.

checklist.step: Report the quarterly results to the Compliance Committee
actions: Prepare the quarterly pack: population counts, sample composition, defect rate by branch and by representative, senior-investor findings, exchange-velocity breaches and open remediation.
Show the trend across the last four quarters so a deteriorating branch is visible rather than a single-quarter number.
Table the pack at the next Compliance Committee sitting and record the minute reference and any committee direction.
Distribute the branch extracts to each supervising principal with their own numbers named.
checklist.done: a four-quarter trended pack is tabled with a recorded minute reference and per-branch extracts distributed.

checklist.step: Roll the quarters into the annual Rule 3120 supervisory controls report
actions: Consolidate the four quarterly tests into the Rule 3120 report covering the supervisory controls tested, the results, any significant compliance problems identified and the amendments made to the WSPs in response.
State the tests performed on the senior-investor stratum and the Rule 2330(d) exchange surveillance explicitly, since these are the areas examiners open on.
Present the report to senior management and record the presentation date and attendees.
Sign the report and file it with the quarterly workpapers as the annual evidence set.
checklist.done: a signed Rule 3120 report consolidates the four quarters, names the WSP amendments made and records the senior-management presentation date.

checklist.step: Retain the supervisory testing evidence
actions: Archive the population extracts, reconciliations, risk-ranking output, sample seed log, per-transaction review notes, branch inspection reports, heightened-supervision plans and the signed conclusions by quarter and branch.
Apply the six-year SEC Rule 17a-4(b) retention label and hold the branch inspection reports per Rule 3110(c)(2).
Confirm the index supports retrieval by quarter, branch, representative CRD and contract number for exam response.
Test retrieval each quarter by reproducing one prior quarter's sample from its recorded seed.
checklist.done: the quarter's evidence is archived under a six-year label, retrievable by branch and CRD, and a prior sample has been reproduced from its seed.

testing.step: Rebuild the quarterly population independently
actions: Write an independent query against the VA transaction tables for the quarter rather than re-running the compliance team's query, and compare row counts.
Confirm subsequent purchase payments, replacements and transactions from terminated representatives are all present.
Recompute customer age at the transaction date and compare the derived senior stratum to the one compliance used.
List and investigate every row present in one population and not the other before proceeding.
testing.done: an independently built population reconciles to the compliance population with every difference explained.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record
actions: Match the population to the insurers' issued-contract confirmations on contract number and to the commission ledger on representative CRD and premium.
List any contract that was issued or paid a commission and is absent from the supervisory population — those transactions were never reviewed.
Reconcile total premium across the three sources and explain any variance above 1%.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the workpaper as the completeness evidence.
testing.done: population, issued contracts and commissions reconcile item for item and in total, with a signed completeness note.

testing.step: Draw the independent overlay sample
actions: Take 100% of population rows absent from the compliance sample that met a mandatory-inclusion rule — senior stratum, threshold breach, open-finding representative.
Take 20 rows the compliance team reviewed and passed, by seeded random selection, to re-perform their judgement.
Take 100% of branches whose defect rate exceeded 10% for the branch inspection test.
Record the seed, strata and draw date so the overlay sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the overlay sample is reproducible and covers every mandatory-inclusion row the compliance sample missed.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk ranking and the sampling arithmetic
actions: Rebuild the risk score for 25 rows from the documented factor weights and compare to the published score, investigating any difference.
Recompute the sampling rate actually achieved — sample rows divided by population rows — and compare to the rate stated in SUP-3120.
Confirm the senior stratum was taken at 100% by comparing the derived senior count to the reviewed senior count.
Redraw the compliance sample from its recorded seed and confirm it reproduces exactly — a non-reproducible sample invalidates the quarter.
testing.done: risk scores, the achieved sampling rate and the 100% senior coverage are recomputed and the compliance sample reproduces from its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the supervisory judgement on passed transactions
actions: Open each overlay-sampled transaction with the compliance disposition hidden and reach an independent conclusion on Rule 2111 and the Reg BI care obligation.
Reveal the recorded disposition and record every case where a Satisfactory was given on a file with an unevidenced profile field or an unquantified exchange.
Test whether the typed reason is specific to the customer or repeated verbatim across files — boilerplate reasons are a supervisory failure in themselves.
Capture the reviewed screens into the workpaper with the ticket id visible.
testing.done: each re-performed transaction has an independent conclusion, a comparison to the recorded disposition and a boilerplate test result.

testing.step: Re-perform the Rule 2330(d) exchange surveillance computation
actions: Recompute per representative the exchange count, the exchange share of VA transactions and the inside-36-month exchange count from the raw transaction data.
Compare to the published surveillance output and list any representative whose breach the production report missed.
Confirm every published breach received a written principal explanation inside 5 business days and read the explanations for adequacy.
Treat a threshold quietly widened without a WSP amendment as a control-design finding.
testing.done: exchange-velocity metrics are independently recomputed, missed breaches are listed and every breach has a timely written explanation.

testing.step: Test the branch inspection module against Rule 3110(c)
actions: Confirm every branch meeting the inspection trigger received a dated inspection report inside the quarter.
Read three reports and confirm they cover the Rule 3110(c)(2) minimum content — safeguarding of funds, account records, supervisory review of transactions and correspondence, and complaint handling.
Confirm the inspection was performed by someone not supervising that branch and not compensated on its production.
Trace three findings from an inspection report through to a GRC issue and a closure date.
testing.done: every triggered branch has a compliant, independently performed inspection report whose findings trace to closed issues.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline and threshold maths for the quarter
actions: Compare the population build date to the first business day after quarter end and the signed conclusion date to quarter end plus 30 calendar days.
Recompute the defect rate by branch and by representative from the raw disposition data and compare to the 2% and 10% thresholds.
Recompute the rolling four-quarter finding count per representative and confirm every representative at three or more sits under a heightened-supervision plan.
List any threshold breach that did not produce the required escalation, with the day count of delay.
testing.done: build and completion dates, defect rates and rolling finding counts are independently recomputed against every stated threshold.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception carrying the quarter, branch, representative CRD, contract number where applicable, the rule implicated and the customer impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — incomplete population, missed mandatory-inclusion row, boilerplate disposition, unescalated threshold breach, overdue inspection — and name an owner.
For exceptions showing an unreviewed customer transaction, open a catch-up review of that transaction and a customer-impact assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's overlay sample as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a listed root cause, a named owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the results
actions: Compute the overlay exception rate and the count of unreviewed mandatory-inclusion transactions against the zero threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting each finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who supervised none of the sampled transactions and reports outside Distribution, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee, record the minute reference, and carry the findings into the annual Rule 3120 supervisory controls report presented to senior management.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the overlay exception rate and the unreviewed-transaction count, with a committee minute reference.
